added_claim_errors: “Unused carryover still expires later” implies mandatory expiration; continued carryover can preserve unused funds in subsequent years.
“Many plans offer neither” is an unsupported prevalence claim.
“Carried into next year (best case) ~$680” misleadingly excludes a grace period preserving access to all $1,900 for timely March care.
Carryover requires being “still enrolled in the FSA in the new plan year”: presented as universal, although enrollment requirements depend on the plan.
“If you change jobs, the whole balance ... is gone” omits the FSA COBRA exception.
“You usually have until March–April to submit receipts” adds an unverified typical deadline; the plan sets its run-out deadline.

reasons: A provides clearer conditional instructions and explicitly warns that December prepayment cannot cover March services. B initially misframes the maximum carryover as the best possible outcome, then adds unsupported enrollment and job-change restrictions, although it later recognizes the grace-period alternative. The arithmetic is $1,900 − $680 = $1,220; A gives the correct formula but an imprecise concluding range, while B gives the correct subtraction without a clear minimum spend-down instruction. Both omit the 2027 open-enrollment recommendation, and B is unnecessarily long for a quick plan.
